findings.title: Cache status ignores the calendar-cache feature flag; repository always hits the DB
findings.body: The handler instantiates `CalendarCacheRepository` directly. The codebase uses `CalendarCache.init` to choose between the real repository and `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the cache is disabled, and this PR adds `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` to the mock. Because the mock is never used here, that method is dead code. It also means the UI can show cache status for deployments or users where caching is disabled.

findings.title: In-memory delegation credentials have negative IDs and are passed to the DB query
findings.body: `connectedCalendars` can contain in-memory delegation credentials with negative or non-DB `credentialId` values. These are passed to `groupBy ... credentialId IN (...)`. Negative IDs never match, so it is wasteful at best. Check that `credentialId` is always a number for these entries, and filter out in-memory delegation IDs before querying.

findings.title: Cache actions are not gated by disableConnectionModification or delegation
findings.body: `hasCache` depends only on integration type and `cacheUpdatedAt`. The dropdown therefore exposes "Delete cached data" even when `disableConnectionModification` is true (for example when the scope is disabled for the event type) or the credential is a delegation credential. A delegation credential's `credentialId` is negative, so the server rejects the deletion with a generic error. Cache deletion should respect the same permission flags as disconnecting.

findings.title: After cache deletion the status is not refetched; onSuccess is optional and unrelated to the cache query
findings.body: `deleteCacheMutation` has no `onSettled` or `onSuccess` invalidation of `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, unlike the disconnect mutation. It relies on the optional `onSuccess` prop, which is `props.onChanged` and may be undefined. The query uses `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, so after a successful delete the dropdown keeps showing the stale "Last updated" timestamp and the delete action. The user can then delete repeatedly.

findings.title: Generic Error is thrown instead of a TRPCError
findings.body: A plain `Error` becomes an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) and is reported as a server error. A missing or unauthorized credential should throw `TRPCError` with code NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN. The router input is also an inline `z.object` rather than a schema file, which is inconsistent with the sibling procedures.

findings.title: Writes to every SelectedCalendar of the credential for no functional purpose
findings.body: `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` runs on every cache refresh, which includes webhook-triggered refreshes. With empty data, Prisma's `@updatedAt` bumps `updatedAt` on all selected calendars of the credential, including rows for other integrations or event types. This adds write load. The PR's own notes say the frontend does not use `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`, so the extra write has no benefit. It also runs after a loop that may throw, so the semantics are inconsistent.

findings.title: groupBy on credentialId for status is unindexed and runs on every connectedCalendars call
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` aggregates MAX(updatedAt) across all cache rows per credential on every `connectedCalendars` query. This is a hot settings-page query. Each credential can have many cache rows. The `updatedAt` column is not indexed and the aggregate is never cached. The query scans all of a credential's cache rows each time.

findings.title: Migration header comment contradicts the SQL
findings.body: The "Warnings" comment says the column was added without a default and that this is not possible on a non-empty table, but the statement adds it with `DEFAULT NOW()`. Existing rows all get the migration timestamp as `updatedAt`, so the UI will show a misleading "last updated" time for old caches.

findings.title: Unrelated dev script uses macOS-only sed -i '' and is outside the PR scope
findings.body: `sed -i ''` fails on GNU/Linux, where `''` is interpreted as the script argument. `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is relative to the current working directory, so the script behaves differently depending on where it is run. The script is unrelated to the feature, and the unrelated `package.json` `ts-node` to `npx tsx` change is in the same category.
